title: Equations with Algebraic Fractions
seo_title: Year 10 Maths: Equations With Fractions Worksheets (GCSE)
standard_text: Solve equations involving algebraic fractions, including those that lead to quadratic equations.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE maths worksheets on solving equations with algebraic fractions that lead to linear and quadratic equations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply every term by the denominators, then solve the quadratic.
key_sub: Reject any answer that makes a denominator 0 or does not make sense.
body_html:
How it works

  • Multiply every term by the denominators (the lowest common multiple of them) to clear the fractions.
  • Expand, collect all terms on one side and solve the quadratic by factorising or the formula.
  • Check each answer: a value that makes a denominator 0 is not allowed. In word problems, also reject answers that do not make sense.
Example

Solve 6x + 4 = 3 + x.

Multiply by (x + 4): 6 = (3 + x)(x + 4)

x² + 7x + 6 = 0, so (x + 1)(x + 6) = 0

Answer: x = −6 or x = −1

Example

Solve 1x + 2x + 1 = 1.

Multiply by x(x + 1): (x + 1) + 2x = x(x + 1)

x² − 2x − 1 = 0, so x = 1 ± √2

Answer: x = −0.41 or x = 2.41

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying only the fractions by the denominator and forgetting the whole-number term.
  • Expanding a minus sign wrongly: −2(x − 3) = −2x + 6.
  • Keeping an answer that makes a denominator 0.
  • In speed problems, subtracting the times the wrong way round. The slower journey takes longer.

faq.a: An equation with the unknown in a denominator, such as 6/(x + 4) = 3 + x. Clearing the fractions often turns it into a quadratic equation.

faq.q: How do you clear the fractions?
faq.a: Multiply every term on both sides by the product (or LCM) of the denominators, then expand and simplify.

faq.q: Why must I check my answers?
faq.a: Multiplying by an expression with x can bring in a value that makes a denominator 0. That value is not a solution and must be rejected.

faq.q: How do I set up a speed word problem?
faq.a: Write each time as distance ÷ speed. The difference between the two times gives the equation, for example 120/x − 120/(x + 10) = 1/2.

sets.title: Equations like a/(x + p) = x + q

items.q: Solve 54x + 1 = x − 2.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 1): 54 = (x + 1)(x − 2). So x2 − x − 56 = 0, which gives x = −7 or x = 8.

items.q: Solve 16x + 5 = x + 5.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 5): 16 = (x + 5)(x + 5). So x2 + 10x + 9 = 0, which gives x = −9 or x = −1.

items.q: Solve 20x + 2 = x + 1.
items.e: Multiply both sides by (x + 2): 20 = (x + 2)(x + 1). So x2 + 3x − 18 = 0, which gives x = −6 or x = 3.

items.e: Multiply both sides by (x − 4): 20 = (x − 4)(x − 3). So x2 − 7x − 8 = 0, which gives x = −1 or x = 8.

items.q: Solve −8x + 5 = x − 1.

sets.title: Two fractions: forming and solving the quadratic

items.q: When −4x − 3x + 3 = −1 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by x(x + 3): −4(x + 3) − 3(x) = −1x(x + 3). Collect terms: x2 − 4x − 12 = 0.

items.q: When 3x + 2 + 2x + 3 = −2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by (x + 2)(x + 3): 3(x + 3) + 2(x + 2) = −2(x + 2)(x + 3). Collect terms: 2x2 + 15x + 25 = 0.

items.q: When −6x − 3 + 5x + 4 = 4 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by (x − 3)(x + 4): −6(x + 4) + 5(x − 3) = 4(x − 3)(x + 4). Collect terms: 4x2 + 5x − 9 = 0.

items.q: When −6x − 2 + 1x + 4 = 2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by (x − 2)(x + 4): −6(x + 4) + 1(x − 2) = 2(x − 2)(x + 4). Collect terms: 2x2 + 9x + 10 = 0.

items.q: When 6x − 3 + 5x + 3 = 1 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by (x − 3)(x + 3): 6(x + 3) + 5(x − 3) = 1(x − 3)(x + 3). Collect terms: x2 − 11x − 12 = 0.

items.q: When 5x + 3 − 1x = 4 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by x(x + 3): 5(x) − 1(x + 3) = 4x(x + 3). Collect terms: 4x2 + 8x + 3 = 0.

items.q: When −2x − 5x + 2 = −3 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: When −4x − 2 − 6x + 4 = −2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: When 2x + 2 + 5x − 1 = 2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by (x + 2)(x − 1): 2(x − 1) + 5(x + 2) = 2(x + 2)(x − 1). Collect terms: 2x2 − 5x − 12 = 0.

items.q: When 6x − 3 + 2x + 4 = 1 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by (x − 3)(x + 4): 6(x + 4) + 2(x − 3) = 1(x − 3)(x + 4). Collect terms: x2 − 7x − 30 = 0.

items.q: When 6x + 1 + 5x + 4 = 2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?
items.e: Multiply every term by (x + 1)(x + 4): 6(x + 4) + 5(x + 1) = 2(x + 1)(x + 4). Collect terms: 2x2 − x − 21 = 0.

items.q: When 3x + 4 + 5x + 2 = −2 is written as a quadratic equation, which is correct?

items.q: Solve x = 4x + 12x.
items.e: Multiply both sides by x: x2 = 4x + 12, so x2 − 4x − 12 = 0 and x = −2 or x = 6.

items.q: Which values of x are not allowed in 2x − 4 + 3x − 2 = 3?
items.e: A denominator cannot be 0. x − 4 = 0 gives x = 4, and x − 2 = 0 gives x = 2: x = 2 and x = 4.

items.q: A student solves x2x − 4 = 16x − 4 and gets x = −4 or x = 4. Which answer must be rejected?
items.e: x = 4 makes x − 4 = 0, and you cannot divide by 0. The solution is x = −4 only. Reject x = 4.

items.q: Grace drives 210 km at x km/h. If she drove 15 km/h faster, the journey would take 20 minutes less. Which equation is correct, and what is x?
c: 210x − 210x + 15 = 20, so x = 45
210x − 210x + 15 = 13, so x = 90
210x + 210x + 15 = 13, so x = 75
210x + 15 − 210x = 13, so x = 105
items.e: Time = distance ÷ speed. The slower time minus the faster time is 13 h. Clearing denominators gives a quadratic with a positive root x = 90 (210 ÷ 90 − 210 ÷ 105 = 13).

items.q: Evie drives 495 km at x km/h. If she drove 20 km/h faster, the journey would take 1 hour less. Which equation is correct, and what is x?
c: 495x − 495x + 20 = 60, so x = 45
495x + 20 − 495x = 1, so x = 110
495x + 495x + 20 = 1, so x = 70
495x − 495x + 20 = 1, so x = 90
items.e: Time = distance ÷ speed. The slower time minus the faster time is 1 h. Clearing denominators gives a quadratic with a positive root x = 90 (495 ÷ 90 − 495 ÷ 110 = 1).

items.q: Maya spends £96 on some books at £x each. If each book cost £2 less, she could buy 4 more. What is the price of one book?
items.e: 96x − 2 − 96x = 4. Clearing denominators gives a quadratic in x whose positive root is £8 (12 books at £8, or 16 at £6).

items.q: Poppy spends £360 on some books at £x each. If each book cost £6 less, she could buy 2 more. What is the price of one book?

items.q: A group of x friends share the cost of a £429 gift equally. If 2 of them drop out, each of the others pays £6 more. How many friends were there at first?
items.e: 429x − 2 − 429x = 6. Multiply by x(x − 2) and simplify: 6x2 − 12x − 858 = 0. The positive answer is 13.
